response_content: {"selected_paradigms": ["subgraph_contrast", "reconstruction", "spectral", "clique_density"], "rationale": "The profile is a sparse, high-dimensional bag-of-words graph (feature_dim=12047, feature_sparsity=0.9975) with a power-law degree distribution (is_power_law=true), hubs (max_degree=1881, degree_std=131.5), and moderate clustering (0.3303) — a setting where contextual and structural anomalies coexist. (3) spectral is included on the strongest landmarker evidence: its upper tail jumps sharply (p95=0.1627 -> p99=0.638, ~4x), and spectral_gap=0.9922 indicates well-separated frequencies, so high-frequency outlier nodes are present as a distinct view. (4) clique_density is the deterministic structural companion recommended for sparse high-dim graphs — the power-law/hub structure and moderate clustering make abnormally dense subgraphs plausible, its landmarker shows a separated tail (p99=0.5018), and it covers the structural population the feature-driven views miss. I deliberately drop local_affinity (landmarker saturated at mean 0.9812 with p90=p95=p99=1.0 — no upper-tail separation, not discriminative here) and community (modularity only 0.2421 signals weak community structure that would make a modularity-residual noisy), keeping the four views maximally complementary: local-contrastive, global-reconstruction, spectral-frequency, and pure-structural."}
